data.title: Celltrion Nears KRW 100 Billion Target in Treasury Share Buyback
data.description:
Celltrion ( (KR:068270) ) has provided an announcement.

Celltrion has completed a planned acquisition of 544,299 common treasury shares between Sept. 1 and Sept. 14, 2026, at an average price of KRW 183,722 per share, for a total of about KRW 100 billion. The buyback closely matched the previously announced target amount, and following the transaction Celltrion holds 1,131,226 treasury shares under Article 165-3, equivalent to 0.49% of its outstanding stock, plus an additional 3,396,528 treasury shares held outside that framework, while the largest shareholder’s stake remains unchanged.

The treasury share acquisition underscores Celltrion’s ongoing capital management strategy aimed at enhancing shareholder value and optimizing its equity structure. With the largest shareholder Celltrion Holdings Co., Ltd. maintaining its 60,475,000-share position, the buyback primarily affects the company’s float and balance sheet rather than control dynamics, signaling a confidence in its valuation and providing potential support for its share price in the biopharmaceutical sector.

data.title: AT4 Fast-Tracks Del Sol Refinery Restart to Showcase U.S. Antimony Supply Chain
data.description:
Trigg Mining Ltd. ( (AU:AT4) ) has shared an announcement.

American Tungsten & Antimony has commenced an ahead-of-schedule restart of the leach and electrowinning circuit at its Del Sol Hydromet Refinery in Nevada, using feed from the White Spar Antimony Mine in Arizona to produce antimony flake and ingot. The campaign is designed to physically demonstrate a U.S. domestic mine-to-metal antimony supply chain, enabling product qualification with defense primes, government agencies and other offtakers while minimising capital outlay by operating within existing permits.

Operating data from the restart will underpin expansion studies for Del Sol’s antimony capacity and support applications to U.S. federal critical minerals programs, including ongoing award negotiations with the Department of Energy for the ASCEND-Sb Project. In parallel, tungsten test work using material from Dutch Mountain, Tennessee Mountain and third-party sources continues at Del Sol, reinforcing AT4’s broader strategy to build integrated U.S. supply chains for both antimony and tungsten in response to growing domestic sourcing requirements for defense and high-tech industries.
